draft.title: What influences consumer decisions
card: Price and income
Price is what a good costs. Income is the money a person has to spend. A higher price or a lower income can lead a consumer to buy less, or to choose a cheaper option.
Quality
Quality is how well a product is made and how long it lasts. Some consumers pay more for a product they expect to last.
Advertising
Advertising is paid messages that try to persuade people to buy. It can make a product seem more appealing or more needed than it is.
Other influences
Friends and family, social media and ethical concerns also shape choices. Ethical concerns are beliefs about right and wrong, such as not buying from a business that treats workers badly.
draft.remember: Many things can shape a purchase: money, the product, what others say and do, and personal values.

a.q: Zara wants new headphones. She skips a well-known brand and buys a cheaper pair because her part-time pay is low. Which influence is shaping her choice most?
opts: Price and income
Advertising
Friends and family
Ethical concerns
a.why: Zara's choice is driven by how much money she has and how much the headphones cost. Nothing in the case says an advert, a friend or a belief about right and wrong changed her mind.
a.clue: What does her low pay limit?

b.q: Liam sees many creators on his social media feed wearing a certain brand of trainers. He decides to buy a pair even though his old ones still fit. Which is the best description of what influenced him?
opts: Social media, as he copied what others were wearing
Quality, as his old trainers had worn out
Ethical concerns, as he wanted to support a cause
Income, as he suddenly had more money to spend
b.why: Liam bought after seeing others wearing the brand online, so social media was the influence. His old trainers still fit, so quality is not the reason, and the case gives no sign of a cause or a change in income.
b.clue: What did he see before he decided?

b.best: Social media, as he copied what others were wearing
